title.narrative: Integrated Multi-sectoral response for IDPs in South Wollo Zone, of Amhara Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThe humanitarian situation in the Amhara Region—particularly in South Wollo Zone—remains severe, driven by recurrent conflict, displacement, drought, and the collapse of essential services. More than 646,000 people are internally displaced across Amhara in Thehulederie Woreda alone, the Jari Kutir 1 and Jari Kutir 2 sites host 3,592 highly vulnerable IDPs living in overcrowded, unsafe shelters with minimal access to water, sanitation, and health care. Women, girls, persons with disabilities, and female-headed households face heightened protection and health risks.ltbrgtTo address these life-threatening gaps, Emmanuel Development Association (EDA), in partnership with Self Help Africa (SHA) and Community to Community (C2C), will implement an Integrated Multi-Sectoral Response for IDPs in South Wollo Zone. The six-month intervention combines Emergency Shelter and NFI, WASH, Health, and Nutrition assistance, targeting the most at-risk families in Jari 1 and Jari 2.ltbrgtKey activities include: rehabilitation and solarization of the 55 kW borehole water scheme to ensure sustainable safe-water supply construction of sanitation facilities and desludging of full latrines distribution of WASH and ES/NFI kits to 716 households hygiene promotion through community campaigns and deployment of Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs) to deliver primary care, reproductive health, and mental-health/psychosocial support. The project incorporated CCCM activities such as support registration of IDPs, capacity building for camp committee, Solar Lighting installment, Safety audit, and strengthened community leadership structures.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTargeted screening and treatment for acute malnutrition will reach children under five and pregnant/lactating women, while community volunteers will be trained in hygiene, protection, and accountability.ltbrgtThe project prioritizes gender equality, protection mainstreaming, and disability inclusion by ensuring that water and sanitation facilities are gender-segregated and accessible, community committees are gender-balanced, and GBV risk-mitigation measures are embedded throughout implementation.ltbrgtBy improving access to safe water, sanitation, shelter, and life-saving health and nutrition services, this project will reduce disease transmission, restore dignity, and strengthen community resilience among conflict-affected IDPs and host populations in South Wollo.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtSelf Help Africa, co-applicant of EDA, is uniquely positioned to deliver this intervention effectively, a fact underscored by our recent nomination to serve as the official co-lead for OCHA's Area-Based Coordination platform in South Wollo Zone. This formal leadership role places us at the heart of the humanitarian response in the project's exact target location, ensuring unparalleled coordination with all ltbrgtlt/pgt
